_comment: Alert definitions in OpenObserve (Alerts -> New alert). Alert names must not contain spaces or special characters, so use underscores. Stream: network_syslog. DHCP and DNS run on hera.middlebury.edu and lion.middlebury.edu (lion is zeus: its lines carry zeus-eip in the message). juno and jupiter are the management appliances. Each alert is created twice: a firing alert (this query, template 'keep-efficientip-firing') and '<alert_name>_cleared' (same query, condition '< 1', its own cleared template whose fingerprint hard-codes '<alert_name>'; verified: '< 1' fires on zero rows). See docs/efficientip-openobserve.md. Measured against real data on 2026-10-07.

alerts.sql: SELECT host, regexp_replace(message, '.* via ([^: ]+).*', '\1') AS relay, regexp_replace(message, '.*from ([0-9a-fA-F:]{17}).*', '\1') AS mac, message FROM "network_syslog" WHERE appname = 'dhcpd' AND host IN ('hera.middlebury.edu','lion.middlebury.edu') AND match_all('no free leases') AND message NOT LIKE '%default-netv4%' AND message NOT LIKE '%efault-netv4%' ORDER BY _timestamp DESC LIMIT 1
alerts.measured: WITHOUT the default-netv4 exclusion this matches ~27,000 lines/day (hera and lion answering DHCPDISCOVER on their own interface for the built-in default-netv4 network): never alert on the raw pattern. WITH the exclusions: 6 events in 30 days, 5 of them a real burst on 2026-09-28 10:07 on hera (relay 140.233.107.1, 'cancel load balance to peer failover-dhcp1-smart.middlebury.edu - no free leases').
alerts.note: dhcpd logs the network name, so this is already per shared network. The card shows the most recent matching line.

alerts.sql: SELECT host, regexp_replace(message, '.* via ([^: ]+).*', '\1') AS relay, regexp_replace(message, '.*from ([0-9a-fA-F:]{17}).*', '\1') AS mac, message FROM "network_syslog" WHERE appname = 'dhcpd' AND host IN ('hera.middlebury.edu','lion.middlebury.edu') AND (match_all('exiting') OR match_all('failed') OR match_all('not running')) ORDER BY _timestamp DESC LIMIT 1
alerts.measured: 1 match in 30 days. Quiet enough, but read that one line first to confirm it is a real fault pattern before enabling.

alerts.sql: SELECT host, regexp_replace(message, '.* via ([^: ]+).*', '\1') AS relay, regexp_replace(message, '.*from ([0-9a-fA-F:]{17}).*', '\1') AS mac, message FROM "network_syslog" WHERE appname = 'named' AND host IN ('hera.middlebury.edu','lion.middlebury.edu') AND match_all('failed') AND match_all('exiting') ORDER BY _timestamp DESC LIMIT 1
alerts.measured: 0 matches in 30 days. named does log from both hosts (about 2.4M and 1.3M lines/day), so silence may just mean nothing broke, but the wording is unverified. Find a real named failure line before relying on this.

alerts.sql: SELECT host, regexp_replace(message, '.* via ([^: ]+).*', '\1') AS relay, regexp_replace(message, '.*from ([0-9a-fA-F:]{17}).*', '\1') AS mac, message FROM "network_syslog" WHERE appname = 'named' AND host IN ('hera.middlebury.edu','lion.middlebury.edu') AND match_all('zone') AND (match_all('not loaded') OR match_all('has errors') OR match_all('loading failed')) ORDER BY _timestamp DESC LIMIT 1
alerts.measured: 0 matches in 30 days. Same caveat as DNS Service Failed: wording unverified.
